harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured a secure, persistent SSH tunnel from node2 loopback port 9082 to node1 loopback port 9081. The original application and status document remain unchanged. Recovery after SSH interruption and sequential node restarts was verified.
actions_performed: Created and enabled the inventory status systemd service on node1.
Created dedicated non-login service accounts and a node-generated ED25519 tunnel key.
Restricted SSH access to public-key authentication and local forwarding solely to 127.0.0.1:9081.
Pinned node1’s verified SSH host key on node2.
Created and enabled a restart-enabled tunnel service on node2.
Verified recovery after terminating the active SSH tunnel session.
Restarted node1 and node2 sequentially and verified changed boot identities and full recovery.
Confirmed SELinux remains enforcing and the installed OS release and kernel were preserved.

evidence.requirement: Node1 application is preserved and available only on loopback port 9081
evidence.summary: The application listens on 127.0.0.1:9081, returns the original document hash, and both supplied files retain their original SHA-256 hashes.

evidence.requirement: Node2 persistently exposes the endpoint on loopback port 9082
evidence.summary: The enabled tunnel service listens on 127.0.0.1:9082, uses a protected dedicated key and pinned host key, and has Restart=always with a two-second delay.

evidence.requirement: Other cluster hosts cannot directly access either listener
evidence.summary: Final post-restart tests show both listeners bound only to loopback and all cluster-address access attempts denied.

evidence.requirement: Tunnel recovers after a brief SSH connection interruption
evidence.summary: The dedicated server-side SSH session was terminated; node2 recreated the tunnel with changed PIDs, incremented its restart counter, and restored the original response.
Healthy baseline captured; reboot acknowledged; boot ID changed from 6ab6a71b… to 4a226050…; application, SSH service, data, and node2 tunnel recovered.
Healthy baseline captured; reboot acknowledged; boot ID changed from 19062a82… to 8353fe65…; tunnel, SSH service, original data, and node1 application recovered.
